phases.name: Reconnaissance
phases.description: Confirm the sample is present and genuine, get a fast static overview of what it contains, understand its documented purpose, then run a full disassembly/decompile/capa pass. Add every discrete CLI switch or value-source mechanism as an endpoint via /api/v1/endpoint/.. so later phases have full coverage.

steps.title: Confirm Sample Integrity
steps.description: Confirm the target binary exists in the project folder, is readable and matches the intended sample. Compute cryptographic hashes and basic file typing before any analysis starts. If the file is missing, corrupted, or does not match the expected hash, do not continue this workflow.
steps.examples:
file samples/setx.exe
md5sum / sha1sum / sha256sum samples/setx.exe
Compare against a known-good hash (Microsoft catalog, VirusTotal) if available.

steps.title: Quick Static Survey
steps.description: Run a fast static pass to see the binary's basic shape before deep analysis: format, architecture, sections, entropy, signing status, high-level import overview. Use it to spot packing, tampering or anything unexpected before deeper recon.
steps.examples:
r2 -q -c 'iI;iS entropy' samples/setx.exe
rabin2 -I samples/setx.exe
r2 -q -c 'iI~signed' samples/setx.exe   # embedded Authenticode signature (many system files are catalog-signed instead, so 'false' alone isn't damning)

steps.title: Understand the Target
steps.description: Read the version resource, embedded manifest and strings to identify what this binary is and what it claims to do. Run a quick capa scan for a high-level capability/ATT&CK summary. Build a clear mental model of the tool's documented purpose before hunting for bugs or abuse primitives.
steps.examples:
r2 -q -c 'izz~ascii' samples/setx.exe | grep -i 'microsoft\|copyright\|assemblyIdentity'
capa samples/setx.exe
Locate the usage/help string in .rdata (setx has no live help without a Windows host).

steps.title: Plan Deep Analysis
steps.description: Plan the deep-analysis pass: which functions to decompile with PyGhidra, which imports/xrefs to chase in radare2, and which capa matches deserve a closer look. Prioritize the CLI argument parser and any file, registry or network handling code -- that's where LOLBAS primitives and memory-safety bugs live.
steps.examples:
capa -vv samples/setx.exe   # per-function matches with addresses
r2 -q -c 'aaa;afl~sym' samples/setx.exe   # named/xref'd functions
Pick the argument-parsing function as the first PyGhidra decompile target.

steps.title: Run Deep Analysis
steps.description: Execute the analysis plan: full radare2 disassembly/xref pass, full capa run with -vv for per-function matches, and PyGhidra headless decompilation of the prioritized functions. Note each function's purpose, arguments, and any missing bounds/validation checks.
steps.examples:
r2 -q -c 'aaa;afl;pdf @ sym.wmain' samples/setx.exe
capa -vv samples/setx.exe > work/capa_verbose.txt
GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR=/usr/share/ghidra ~/.local/share/pipx/venvs/pyghidra/bin/python decompile.py  # dump C for arg-parser + Reg*/file-handling functions

steps.title: Add Attack-Surface Units To ShiftGrid
steps.description: Add every discrete CLI switch and value-source mechanism you identified (e.g. bare 'variable value', /K reg:key, /F filename /A x,y,x1,y2, /F filename /R, /F filename /X, /S /U /P /M) as an endpoint via the API, so later phases test each one individually.
steps.examples:
POST /api/v1/endpoint {"name": "/F filename /A x,y,x1,y2", "description": "sets value by reading fixed-offset text from an arbitrary file"}
Repeat for every switch / value-source combination found in the argument parser.

phases.icon: <circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M15 9l-2 4-4 2 2-4 4-2z" fill="currentColor"/>
phases.name: Free Reconnaissance
phases.description: Step back and look for recon gaps the structured steps missed -- undocumented switches, hidden delay-load imports, unusual resource sections, debug-info leakage. Recon only -- no vulnerability testing here.

steps.title: Free-Form Recon
steps.description: Read GET /api/v1/notes and decide if anything is still missing recon-wise: an unexplored delay-load import, an undocumented switch combination, a resource or overlay you have not inspected. Only act on real gaps; otherwise finish with status=skipped.
steps.examples:
Targeted: decompile a DelayLoad_* stub you saw in imports but never traced (e.g. WNetAddConnection2W).
Skipped: status=skipped, observations='Recon already covered every import, section and resource. Nothing missing.'

phases.icon: <circle cx="6" cy="6" r="2" fill="currentColor"/><circle cx="18" cy="6" r="2" fill="currentColor"/><circle cx="12" cy="18" r="2" fill="currentColor"/><path d="M6 8l5 8M18 8l-5 8M8 6h8" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" fill="none" stroke-linecap="round"/>
phases.name: Function & Path Discovery
phases.description: Systematically work through every function and code path in the binary, not just the ones already prioritized, until coverage is complete. Hunt specifically for dead code, unreachable-from-documented-switches branches, and anything that reads like a leftover debug hook, test flag or undocumented feature. Discovery only here -- deep vulnerability testing on what you find happens later.

steps.title: Map Function & Path Coverage
steps.description: Pull the full function list (radare2 `afl` / Ghidra FunctionManager) and compare it against what has already been reviewed this project. Pick the next unreviewed batch, decompile it with PyGhidra, and trace its callers/callees and cross-references. Record what each function does and update the running coverage tally (reviewed vs total) in the notes so the next cycle picks up where this one left off. Pay special attention to: functions with no xrefs (dead or only indirectly-called code), branches never reachable from any documented CLI switch, code gated behind a comparison to a string or flag not seen in the usage text, and anything that looks like a leftover test hook or Easter egg. Write a finding immediately for anything that looks like undocumented functionality or a real bug -- do not wait for a later phase. Only finish the phase early with status=skipped if a full pass found zero new functions and zero anomalies.
steps.examples:
r2 -q -c 'aaa;afl' samples/setx.exe | wc -l   # total function count, compare to your reviewed tally
r2 -q -c 'aaa;afl~^0x' samples/setx.exe > work/all_funcs.txt   # diff against a reviewed-list file each cycle
PyGhidra: decompile the next unreviewed batch from FunctionManager.getFunctions(true)
r2 -q -c 'axt @ fcn.NNNN' samples/setx.exe   # find callers of a function with no obvious caller -- dead code or hidden entry point?
Flag: a branch only reachable via a comparison against a constant string never seen in the /? usage output.

phases._comment: Phase id MUST stay 'general_checks': the workflow page hardcodes that id to render the 'In focus / Recently worked on' checklist panel (workflow.html + routes.py). Renaming it hides the panel.

phases.name: Work on Checklist
phases.description: Tune the project checklist to a native Windows binary: drop anything web-only (SQLi, XSS, CSRF, session/auth-token checks) as not applicable, keep and sharpen memory-safety, unsafe-API-usage and LOLBAS-abuse checks, then work every global-scope check to completion. Ignore the endpoint checks -- they are worked on later.

steps.title: Tune the Checklist
steps.description: Review the checklist against this target. Mark web-only checks 'not applicable' with a one-line reason, and add any binary-analysis check that is missing (e.g. DLL search-order hijacking, format-string usage, integer overflow in offset parsing, anti-analysis behavior). Use the API -- notes alone do not change the checklist.

steps.title: Increase Check Runs
steps.description: Review the checklist against this target. For what checks would it make sense to have a deeper look -- e.g. input validation, memory safety, LOLBAS abuse potential? Increase the runs for these checks to have a very thorough look at them!

steps.title: Work the Global Checks
steps.description: Work every global-scope check. Focus it, do real static (and where possible dynamic) testing instead of trusting old notes, record what you did and found, then finish it. Keep going until every global-check is done. Any bug or LOLBAS primitive you find, immediately write an issue (or update an existing issue) using the /api/v1/finding API!
steps.examples:
POST /api/v1/check/{id}/focus
Decompile the relevant function in PyGhidra, trace bounds checks with r2
PUT /api/v1/check/{id}/observations  {"observations": "..."}
POST /api/v1/check/{id}/finish

phases.name: Switch / Value-Source Testing
phases.description: Pull together every CLI switch and value-source mechanism discovered so far, group them by purpose, then test each one for LOLBAS abuse potential and implementation bugs.

steps.title: Collect Attack-Surface Units
steps.description: Information-gathering only. Review notes, capa output and the decompiled argument parser for every switch / value-source mechanism found so far and add each one through /api/v1/endpoint/.. Do not run new analysis here -- just make coverage complete.
steps.examples:
GET /api/v1/notes
Then POST /api/v1/endpoint for each switch not yet stored (/S, /U, /P, /M, /K, /F, /A, /R, /X, bare variable+value).

steps.title: Group by Purpose
steps.description: Sort the switches into feature groups so related mechanisms are tested together, e.g. 'Value Source' (plain args, /K, /F+/A, /F+/R, /F+/X), 'Remote/Auth' (/S /U /P /M), 'Registry Target' (/K reg:key path parsing).

steps.title: Increase Testing Runs
steps.description: Review the switches for this target. /F (file-sourced value), /A /R /X (offset/regex extraction), and /K (registry-sourced value) are the highest-value targets for both memory-safety bugs and indirect env-var-setting / LOLBAS file-read primitives -- increase runs on these for a very thorough look.

steps.title: Test All Switches
steps.description: Test every switch thoroughly, one feature group at a time. For each one: decompile its handler in PyGhidra, trace input validation and bounds checks in radare2, and determine (a) can it be abused to disclose file or registry contents it shouldn't (LOLBAS file-read/registry-read), (b) can the variable name, target key path, or value be sourced indirectly rather than typed literally on the command line -- avoiding plain-text command-line logging/telemetry, and (c) does offset/length parsing (/A x,y,x1,y2) have integer-overflow or out-of-bounds read risk. Record observations and raw captures, set a status, then mark it tested. Any findings immediately go to /api/v1/finding.
steps.examples:
POST /endpoint/{id}/focus -> POST /endpoint/{id}/checks-adjusted
GET /workflow/endpoint-testing/current-step?endpoint_id={id}
Decompile handler, craft a malicious value-file for /F /A, check bounds
PUT /check/{cid}/observations -> PUT /check/{cid}/status
Loop until done, then POST /endpoint/{id}/unfocus.

phases.icon: <path d="M12 3l2 5 5 2-5 2-2 5-2-5-5-2 5-2 2-5z" fill="currentColor"/><circle cx="19" cy="5" r="1.5" fill="currentColor"/><circle cx="5" cy="19" r="1.5" fill="currentColor"/>
phases.name: Free Testing
phases.description: Anything the structured phases missed? Chase hunches and chain what you have found -- especially around indirect value-sourcing and file/registry read primitives.

steps.title: Refine Notes
steps.description: The notes should not be a simple log of what happened. They should reflect a holistic view: what is this binary's documented use case, and what is the attacker model for a signed, trusted native LOLBIN? What did Microsoft try to accomplish, and where might input validation or command-line-visibility assumptions have been missed? Rewrite the notes to contain both a structured overview of this analysis and this holistic risk view.

steps.title: Free-Form Testing
steps.description: Follow up on anything the structured phases did not cover: a suspicious offset calculation, an unvalidated length, or chaining two earlier findings (e.g. an arbitrary-file-read primitive feeding into a registry write). Record what you try and what comes of it.
steps.examples:
Craft a value-file with a huge /A x2 offset and trace in PyGhidra whether it's bounds-checked.
Test whether /K reg:key can point at HKLM keys the tool shouldn't normally expose.
Check whether the resulting env var's process-visible value can be used to exfiltrate file contents (LOLBAS file read).

phases.icon: <circle cx="11" cy="11" r="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M20 20l-4-4" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round"/><path d="M11 8.5v5M8.5 11h5" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round"/>
phases.name: Additional Work
phases.description: Before writing anything up, do the extra work that pays off: dig deeper where a primitive is likely hiding -- especially the exact mechanics of setting an env var without typing its key, path or value literally -- then prune anything that will not hold up. Only confirmed, reproducible issues should reach Finding Writing.

steps.title: Deep-Dive Where It Pays Off
steps.description: Read GET /api/v1/notes and review the testing so far, then pick the spots where a deeper hunt is worth it -- most importantly, trace exactly which of {variable name, registry key path, value} can be sourced indirectly via /F, /A, /R, /X or /K, and document a concrete working command line for each. Also dig into any half-explored bounds-check or offset-parsing path. If nothing warrants a deeper look, finish with status=skipped.
steps.examples:
Trace the /F /A handler instruction-by-instruction in PyGhidra to confirm exactly which fields must still be typed literally vs. which can come from a file/registry.
Chain a crafted value-file with a registry-write to build a full indirect-persistence PoC.
Skipped: status=skipped, observations='Coverage was thorough; no area warrants a deeper dive.'

steps.title: Identify False Positives
steps.description: Go back over every suspected bug or primitive and reproduce it from scratch. This sample runs in a static-analysis-only Linux environment with no live Windows execution target -- clearly label anything not dynamically confirmed as 'static-analysis-only, unconfirmed dynamically' and reflect that in severity. Discard anything that does not hold up as a false positive; keep a clean reproduction plus evidence for the rest.
steps.examples:
Re-derive the decompiled logic and confirm the control-flow path is actually reachable with attacker-controlled input.
Discard a 'bug' that only appears in an unreachable dead-code branch.
Note clearly if a finding is static-only pending a real Windows VM / Wine confirmation.

phases.icon: <path d="M5 3v18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round"/><path d="M5 4h13l-3 4 3 4H5" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linejoin="round"/>
phases.name: Finding Writing
phases.description: Turn every confirmed bug or LOLBAS primitive into a clear, evidenced finding.

steps.title: Write Up Findings
steps.description: Create a finding for every confirmed bug or abuse primitive with a clear title, a severity and a description of impact and reproduction. Attach the supporting raw captures (decompiled code, disassembly, capa output, PoC commands) so each finding stands on its own. The description should start with 1) What is the problem in simple non-technical words, then 2) A 'so-what' section that explains why this is a problem (e.g. command-line-logging evasion, arbitrary file/registry read), then 3) more technical details. The recommendation should offer the proper fix and quick mitigations as an alternative.
steps.examples:
POST /api/v1/finding  {"title": "setx /F /A allows env var value to be sourced from an arbitrary file without appearing in the command line", "severity": "medium", "description": "..."}
PUT /api/v1/finding/{id}/raw-captures  (attach decompiled snippet + PoC)

steps.title: Attach Evidence for Medium+ Findings
steps.description: Every finding rated medium, high or critical must carry at least one piece of visual evidence. Review each finding's severity and attach a raw capture for any that is medium or higher -- a Ghidra decompiler/graph screenshot, an r2 disassembly capture, or a terminal capture of the PoC running. Findings rated info or low do not require one. This is important. Make sure you really capture it!
steps.examples:
GET /api/v1/findings  (review each finding's severity)
POST /api/v1/finding/{id}/raw-captures  (attach a Ghidra screenshot or PoC terminal capture for each medium-or-higher finding)
